# Cases compared against llvm-mc alone.
#
# A sign-extended 32-bit absolute field (R_X86_64_32S in ELF): llvm-mc writes
# IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR32, the only 32-bit absolute type the PE specification
# has, and rsasm follows it. GNU as writes type 17, which the specification
# names IMAGE_REL_AMD64_SSPAN32 and BFD uses for its own purposes.
=== sign-extended immediate
        movq    $foo, %rax
=== sign-extended displacement
        movl    foo, %eax
        movl    foo+4(,%rax,8), %ecx
# GNU as for mingw reads `@GOTPCREL` as part of the symbol's name; llvm-mc
# takes it as the plain RIP-relative reference it is in a Windows object.
=== GOTPCREL
        movq    foo@GOTPCREL(%rip), %rax
# A call to a function (`.type 32`) in its own section: llvm-mc keeps the
# relocation, for the MSVC linker's incremental linking and control flow
# guard; GNU as resolves it like any other local reference.
=== def, scl and type
        .text
        .def    func
        .scl    2
        .type   32
        .endef
        .globl  func
func:   ret
        .def    helper
        .scl    3
        .type   32
        .endef
helper: ret
        call    helper
# Weak symbols. A weak definition becomes an undefined weak external whose
# fallback is a global under a made-up name, `.weak.<name>.default.<first
# global defined in the object>`; GNU as leaves out `.default`. A reference to
# a weak definition in its own section is resolved by llvm-mc, which GNU as
# relocates.
=== weak definition and reference
        .text
        .globl  first
first:  ret
        .weak   w
w:      ret
        call    w
        .weak   wu
        call    wu
        .quad   w, wu
=== weak with no global defined
        .text
        call    undef
        .weak   w
w:      ret
=== weak data
        .data
        .weak   wd
wd:     .long   1
        .globl  after
after:  .long   wd
# COMDAT sections, which GNU as writes with a symbol order and alignment of
# its own.
=== comdat any
        .section .text$f,"xr",discard,f
        .globl  f
f:      ret
        .section .rdata$c,"dr",same_size,c
        .globl  c
c:      .long   4
        .text
        call    f
=== comdat selections
        .section .s1,"dr",one_only,s1
        .globl  s1
s1:     .byte   1
        .section .s3,"dr",same_contents,s3
        .globl  s3
s3:     .byte   3
        .section .s4,"dr",largest,s4
        .globl  s4
s4:     .byte   4
        .section .s5,"dr",newest,s5
        .globl  s5
s5:     .byte   5
=== linkonce
        .section .lo,"dr"
        .linkonce discard
lo:     .long   5
        .section .lo2,"dr"
        .linkonce same_size
        .long   6
# Unwind data for x86-64 functions. llvm-mc counts the prologue from the
# instructions' lengths, which GNU as does too, but writes `.xdata` and
# `.pdata` aligned to four bytes and names the function's section rather than
# the function in `.pdata`.
=== seh frame
        .text
        .globl  f
        .def    f; .scl 2; .type 32; .endef
        .seh_proc f
f:
        pushq   %rbp
        .seh_pushreg %rbp
        subq    $32, %rsp
        .seh_stackalloc 32
        movq    %rsp, %rbp
        .seh_setframe %rbp, 0
        .seh_endprologue
        nop
        addq    $32, %rsp
        popq    %rbp
        ret
        .seh_endproc
=== seh two functions
        .text
        .seh_proc f
f:      pushq   %rbp
        .seh_pushreg %rbp
        .seh_endprologue
        popq    %rbp
        ret
        .seh_endproc
        .seh_proc g
g:      pushq   %rbx
        .seh_pushreg %rbx
        pushq   %r12
        .seh_pushreg %r12
        .seh_endprologue
        popq    %r12
        popq    %rbx
        ret
        .seh_endproc
=== seh large allocations and saves
        .text
        .seh_proc big
big:
        subq    $4096, %rsp
        .seh_stackalloc 4096
        movq    %rsi, 16(%rsp)
        .seh_savereg %rsi, 16
        movaps  %xmm6, 32(%rsp)
        .seh_savexmm %xmm6, 32
        subq    $0x100000, %rsp
        .seh_stackalloc 0x100000
        .seh_endprologue
        ret
        .seh_endproc
=== seh handler
        .text
        .seh_proc h
h:      pushq   %rbp
        .seh_pushreg %rbp
        .seh_handler handler, @except, @unwind
        .seh_endprologue
        ret
        .seh_endproc
=== seh handler data
        .text
        .seh_proc h
h:      subq    $8, %rsp
        .seh_stackalloc 8
        .seh_endprologue
        .seh_handler handler, @except
        .seh_handlerdata
        .long   0x1234
        .text
        ret
        .seh_endproc
=== seh pushframe
        .text
        .seh_proc isr
isr:    .seh_pushframe @code
        .seh_endprologue
        iretq
        .seh_endproc
=== associative comdat
        .section .text$f,"xr",discard,f
        .globl  f
f:      ret
        .section .xdata$f,"dr",associative,f
        .long   1
        .section .data$d,"dw",associative,f
        .long   f
